title: Incremental canary, cost-aware safety checks, and state reconciliation for config changes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Build an automated, conservative config-apply system that performs incremental canaries for batching and caching recommendations, enforces cost-aware guardrails, and provides a deterministic state reconciliation path with automatic safe rollback. Scope: canary engine, cost delta gating, health signal aggregation, reconciliation controller, audit logging and operator overrides. Out of scope: UI redesign for Console dashboards (will add follow-up ticket). Rationale: Previous incidents show broad config flips can spike latency or increase token cost for bursty workloads. An incremental canary with explicit cost and latency gates reduces blast radius while enabling automated gains from batching/kv-cache changes.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Kickoff meeting: aligned on three major safety checks: error-rate, p95 latency, and per-token cost delta. Action: infra to provide baseline metrics for last 7d.
2026-02-18 - Design review (PM + SRE): PM requested an operator-visible canary window and opt-in auto-rollback. SRE requested stronger hysteresis to avoid flip-flop during transient infra noise.
2026-02-22 - Engineering note: implemented canary percent ramper and a lightweight dry-run mode that computes simulated cost impact without changing live routing.
2026-02-25 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/12567 contains the canary controller and reconciliation state machine. Needs load test telemetry and SLO math in observability layer.
2026-02-27 - PM feedback on acceptance criteria: require both cost and p95 checks to pass for at least two consecutive canary windows before promoting to 100%.
Next steps: integrate with Optimize recommendation engine to mark recommendations as 'auto-apply eligible' after manual review; add dashboard tiles for canary health and cost delta.
acceptance_criteria: Canary controller can perform staged rollouts: 1%, 5%, 25%, 100% with configurable dwell time
Automated gating: if error-rate > 0.5% OR p95 latency increases > 20% OR cost per 1M tokens increases > 8% vs baseline, canary aborts and triggers rollback
Reconciliation controller converges to desired config within 5 minutes after controller restart and logs state transitions to audit log
Dry-run mode produces a simulated cost delta and predicted latency impact without changing traffic routing
Operator UI link and runbook created for manual override and forced promote/rollback
End-to-end tests and load tests demonstrating rollback triggers under synthetic noise are present in CI
implementation_notes: Model: represent a config apply as an immutable change set with an idempotent reconcile loop. Each change set carries metadata: batch_size_hint, kv_cache_policy, quantization_profile, recommendation_id, and expected cost_delta_pct.
Canary ramp: built-in schedule (1m dwell per step in staging, 10m in production) and exponential backoff on transient failures. Percent steps configurable per project.
Gating signals: aggregate error-rate, p95 latency, and cost-per-1M-tokens from the Console metrics store. Use moving-window comparisons (5m window vs 1h baseline) to reduce sensitivity to outliers.

Hysteresis: require two consecutive windows passing thresholds before promoting; require two windows failing before rollback. Also incorporate derived signal: error_rate * latency_increase to catch correlated regressions.
Rollback action: route traffic to last-known-good variant and mark change-set state as 'Reverted' with a reason code. Persist revert action and link to triggering windows for postmortem.

KV cache-specific: when enabling more aggressive prefix caching, run a synthetic workload in dry-run that exercises common prefixes and estimates hit-rate delta; if predicted memory pressure > configured threshold, block promotion.

Cost-awareness: use cost-model hooks from Optimize to compute baseline and projected per-token cost; only auto-promote recommendations with projected savings > configurable minimum (default 4%) to avoid noisy churn.
Observability: emit canary lifecycle events (Started, StepReached, GateFailed, Promoted, Reverted) to event bus and Console so operators can filter and trace.
Safety: support 'suspend auto-apply' label per workspace and a global kill-switch controlled by SRE with audit logging. All actions require signed operator token for manual override.
test_plan: Unit tests for reconcile state transitions and idempotency
Integration tests: dry-run vs live apply for a sample batching change set
Load tests: synthetic chat workloads to validate p95/throughput under canary and full-promote paths
Chaos test: introduce transient infra latency and validate hysteresis prevents flip-flop
Cost simulation: run Optimize's cost model on historical traces to validate projected vs observed cost delta within +/- 2%
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature flag off in prod, deploy controller to prod cluster and run in dry-run for 72h against small traffic subset
Phase 1: enable canary controller in passive mode for all workspaces (no auto-promote), surface canary metrics in Console
Phase 2: opt-in workspaces only - support beta customers, monitor for 2 weeks
Phase 3: enable auto-promote for recommendations meeting 'auto-apply eligible' criteria and runbook reviewed
Rollback: operator-triggered immediate revert and automated revert on gate failure. Postmortem for any revert with customer-visible impact > low
estimated_savings: up to 12% per-token cost for chat-heavy workloads after enabling batching + kv-cache recommendations; typical safe baseline target 4-6%
